question: Your customer support agent's evaluation set marks each conversation as passed when the agent chose the right outcome: refund, denial, or escalation. When the results are broken down by request type, every type scores at least 93%, including billing disputes. The team now plans to let the agent call process_refund for billing disputes without human approval. Which step should you take next?

options.text: Review only the conversations marked as failed, because the conversations that passed already showed correct handling and need no further checking before approval is removed.
options.reason: A wrong refund amount can sit inside a conversation that passed on its outcome, so the failed conversations cannot reveal it; the field itself must be measured.

options.text: Replace the per-type scores with the single overall score, because small per-type groups are less reliable than one figure covering the whole set.
options.reason: The guide warns that aggregate accuracy can mask poor performance on specific segments, so dropping the breakdown removes the check that the guide requires.

options.text: Measure the accuracy of the refund amount field separately, because a pass covers only the chosen outcome and can hide wrong amounts inside the high score.
options.reason: Aggregate accuracy can mask poor performance on specific fields, so accuracy must be validated per field as well as per type before high-confidence actions are automated.

options.text: Add more billing disputes until they form half of the evaluation set, so that the overall score reflects them more strongly before approval is removed.
options.reason: Reweighting the set still yields one aggregate number, and an aggregate can mask poor performance on a specific field such as the refund amount.
